question.text: An overnight fund would most likely be placed at which level of the Risk-o-meter?

explanation.text: The Logic: Overnight funds invest in securities that mature in one business day, so duration and credit exposure are minimal. Because the Risk-o-meter labels schemes from "Low" through "Very High" based on the underlying portfolio's risk profile, a portfolio of one-day instruments is generally placed at the "Low" end of the scale — the lowest band available on the meter. The Trap: "High", "Very High", and "Moderately High" describe equity-oriented or longer-duration debt schemes whose portfolio risk is materially greater than one-day money. Overnight funds, sitting at the shortest possible maturity, do not belong in any of those bands. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B (MFF) workbook states that overnight funds invest in one-day securities and that liquid/money-market funds are among the lowest-risk categories, and separately describes the Risk-o-meter as a scheme-risk disclosure, but the pages checked do not explicitly assign the "Low" label to overnight funds. The placement above reflects general industry/regulatory practice.
